driven: sp_ready (bits [Sp2VWidth-1:0] driven by ready_o or ready_no)
sp_ctr_we (bits [Sp2VWidth-1:0] driven by ctr_we_o or ctr_we_no)

guarantees.claim: For every i in 0..Sp2VWidth-1, an instance of aes_ctr_fsm_p (if SP2V_LOGIC_HIGH[i]==1) or aes_ctr_fsm_n (otherwise) is instantiated and its outputs directly drive sp_ready[i], mr_alert[i], mr_ctr_slice_idx[i], mr_ctr_o_slice[i], and sp_ctr_we[i].
Every FSM instance receives clk_i, rst_ni, sp_incr[i], incr_err, mr_err, and ctr_i_slice; the connectivity is fixed at elaboration.

assumptions.claim: The outputs mr_alert[i], mr_ctr_slice_idx[i], and mr_ctr_o_slice[i] from all i must be OR-combined externally to produce the final single-bit or single-slice signals.
assumptions.cond: when any FSM asserts alert or outputs slice index/data
assumptions.risk: If OR combination is not performed, a single instance's signal may be taken as the final value, missing alerts or misrouting control data from other slices.

assumptions.claim: SP2V_LOGIC_HIGH must be a bitvector of width Sp2VWidth with each bit either 1'b1 or 1'b0, matching the compilation scope.
assumptions.risk: Mismatch would cause a compilation error; if passed, partially uninstantiated bits would leave outputs undriven.

assumptions.claim: The sparsified signals sp_incr and sp_ctr_we respect the encoding where SP2V_LOGIC_HIGH[i]==1 indicates the 'positive' instance and 0 the 'negative' instance; the rest of the design must maintain this convention.
assumptions.risk: If the mapping is inverted relative to other sparsity logic, the redundant FSM instances may not detect faults correctly, degrading security.

uncertain_points.claim: The OR-combination of mr_alert, mr_ctr_slice_idx, and mr_ctr_o_slice across all i is not implemented in this chunk; verify that the parent module correctly OR-reduces these per-bit signals.
uncertain_points.risk: An alert or critical slice identifier from one slice could be missed, allowing a fault to propagate unhandled.

uncertain_points.claim: The internal logic of aes_ctr_fsm_p vs aes_ctr_fsm_n is not visible; verify that the two modules are exact functional complements under sparsity so that any divergence (e.g., in error handling) is detectable via OR-combine.
uncertain_points.risk: If the modules contain mismatched error logic, a fault may not be flagged consistently, potentially allowing undetected counter manipulation.

uncertain_points.claim: The inputs incr_err and mr_err are connected identically to all instances; confirm they are toggled under fault conditions and that the FSM instances use them (otherwise errors may be silently ignored).
uncertain_points.cond: when an increment or masking error occurs
uncertain_points.risk: If these error signals are tied low or unused inside the FSM, real errors would not generate alerts.
